group_assessment.weighting: A genetic-epidemiology group running a candidate-set germline association in a registry case-control study of childhood glioma; WWOX is one of 1318 genes entering through a Gene Ontology label, not a hypothesis of the group. Observation (case-control counts, odds ratios) is weighted above interpretation (mitochondrial energy insufficiency in childhood glioblastoma), which has no functional readout behind it.

field_density.note: Record matches, not measurements; the rs62036057 query returns this paper alone.

resolved.how: Ref 32 (Watanabe 2003), the only source the paper gives for WWOX mitochondrial localisation and brain expression, resolved at ABSTRACT level only (PubMed EFetch 2026-10-19; no PMC deposit, no DOI on the PubMed record, Europe PMC inEPMC N): the abstract reports WWOX associated mainly with mitochondria before confluence in one human fibroblast line and nuclear after confluence, and reports WWOX in non-cancerous epithelial cells only; it does not mention brain. Not a reading and no receipt is claimed; the full text was not acquired.

queued.why: Full text of ref 32 (Watanabe 2003) not acquired (cascade: PubMed link-out, Europe PMC, DOI lookup by title in Crossref returned an unrelated record); refs 33 (Kuroki 2002, no receipt) and 34 (Paige 2001, partial receipt only) not read. No conclusion of this reading rests on them.

entries.proposition: Design: registry-based case-control study, genotyping from archived dried blood spots on a SNP array, European and Hispanic children analysed separately.
entries.snippet: Subjects were derived from the California Childhood Cancer Records Linkage Project (CCRLP), a case-control study

entries.proposition: The glioblastoma stratum is small: 44 European and 43 Hispanic cases against 1431 and 1501 controls.
entries.snippet: Association analyses were conducted in self-reported Hispanics (43 cases and 1501 controls) and Europeans (44 cases and 1431 controls) separately

entries.proposition: WWOX enters the analysis only as a member of a Gene Ontology mitochondrion gene set (about 1300 genes), not as a candidate chosen for WWOX biology.
entries.snippet: SNPs bounded by their genomic coordinates within this GO category were included in N-mt SNP scanning.
entries.anchor: Methods, N-mt Gene Set Association Analysis

entries.proposition: The European significance threshold for the nuclear-mitochondrial scan is 6.28e-6 and the meta-analysis threshold 5.63e-6.
entries.anchor: Methods, N-mt Gene Set Association Analysis

entries.proposition: The WWOX result: rs62036057 reached OR 2.99, P 3.42e-6 in Europeans, just under the Bonferroni threshold.
entries.snippet: In European children, rs62036057 was significant after Bonferroni correction (OR = 2.99, 95% CI 1.88–4.75, P-value = 3.42 X 10–6)

entries.proposition: The SNP is intronic and the association is absent in Hispanic children and in the meta-analysis.
entries.snippet: However, the association with this SNP was not statistically significant in the analysis limited to Hispanic children nor in the meta-analysis

entries.proposition: Table S7 row for WWOX: European OR 2.99 (P 3.42e-6), Hispanic OR 1.3 (P 0.37), meta-analysis OR 2.14 (P 3.07e-5, above the 5.63e-6 threshold); the table does not name the effect allele.
Table S7 row for EFHD1 reports Hispanic OR 6.19 and meta-analysis OR 3.57 (the abstract attaches the 3.57 value to the Hispanic stratum).
Fig 2 legend gives the genomic inflation factor of the European Q-Q plot as 1.30.
entries.snippet: (B) Q-Q plot for European subjects (lambda value = 1.30)

entries.proposition: Figure 2A/B: in the European Manhattan plot a single point near chromosome 16 clears the threshold line by a small margin, and the Q-Q plot departs upward only in its top tail; no regional association plot, no effect allele and no allele frequency is shown for the WWOX SNP.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2A-B (European): Manhattan plot with a red Bonferroni line near -log10 p 5.2; one point above the line on the chromosome 16 band at about 5.5, other chromosome points below; Q-Q plot with observed points on the diagonal until the last few points at -log10 expected above about 3.5, which rise above the line.

entries.proposition: The mitochondrial m1555 variant is found in only three glioblastoma cases and is described by the authors as unlikely sufficient on its own.
entries.snippet: Indeed, only 3 subjects of our case group carry this variant.

entries.proposition: Figure 1A: in Europeans the m1555 point sits below the Bonferroni line (about 3.5 against about 3.7), i.e. the European stratum alone does not clear it; only the meta-analysis panel C does.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 1A-C: scatter of -log10 p against mtDNA position, red line near 3.7; panel A highest point about 3.5 below the line; panel B no point near the line; panel C one point about 3.9 above the line at about position 1500.

entries.proposition: The WWOX statement of mitochondrial localisation is sourced to a single reference; the paper offers no mitochondrial measurement of its own.
entries.snippet: WWOX protein localizes to the mitochondria

entries.proposition: The authors read the WWOX germline hit as support for carcinogenesis rather than treatment effects; the design measures neither expression nor function.
entries.snippet: Our findings at the germline level lend support to the former hypothesis.

entries.proposition: The authors name the absence of replication and the small sample as the major drawback.
entries.snippet: One major drawback of our study is the lack of a replication dataset.
